title: General-purpose fabric that retires data-movement dominance

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a programmable computer that places processing within or close to stored data and coordinates that processing so effectively that transporting data between separate memory and compute units no longer dominates whole-system energy across diverse applications. The target includes end-to-end database programs, graph analytics, scientific computing, and neural networks, together with the software support needed to run them. It is a proposed system capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Processing near memory and computing within memory already exist, including commercial, highly programmable processing-in-memory systems. Consequently, neither co-location nor programmability alone distinguishes this innovation. Its defining advance would be broad application execution with measured removal of transport-energy dominance at the system level. A specialized multiply-accumulate tile demonstrates a useful primitive, but does not by itself demonstrate this broader capability.

significance.text: Conventional architectures separate memory and processing, making repeated transfers of operands and results costly for data-intensive work. A broadly programmable fabric that substantially reduces these costs while delivering large system-level efficiency improvements would be a major computer-architecture advance. The novelty would lie in making an existing architectural principle work across complete applications and their supporting software, rather than in first inventing computation near stored data. The stored-program model itself does not require physically distant processing and memory.

Lower transport energy would follow directly from achieving the target, but large throughput gains would require separate evidence. Moving work toward memory can expose a new compute bottleneck: the UPMEM study reports that many evaluated local workloads become compute-bound. Even a substantial improvement in energy-delay product can coexist with increased execution time if energy falls sufficiently. Energy consumption, execution time, and throughput therefore need separate reporting.

Conditional synthesis: if savings survive communication, control, accuracy management, and software overheads, the fabric could make large data workloads more practical within power and cooling budgets. Wider deployment would also depend on usable compilers, runtimes, operating-system integration, and reliability. The supplied evidence motivates this engineering work, but does not establish that every component requires a further fundamental breakthrough or that all application classes would benefit equally.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unresolved target is integrated, broad software execution with consistently low transport-energy costs, rather than an isolated memory-side operation. Bank-local processing can reduce some transfers while leaving communication between processing units expensive. In the documented UPMEM architecture, threads on different data processing units cannot directly share data or synchronize; communication must pass through the host. A successful fabric would need to handle application-wide data exchange and synchronization without allowing those paths to erase local savings.

Analog in-memory computing offers another route, but its arithmetic must contend with noise, device and circuit variation, and other non-idealities. The January 2026 review discusses precision improvement through techniques including bit slicing, residue arithmetic, and iterative refinement. Analog computation should therefore not be described as inherently limited to approximate outputs: higher precision can be obtained, but with tradeoffs in area, complexity, digital processing, and related overheads. The engineering challenge is to retain a system-level benefit after paying for the accuracy an application requires.

Programming and system integration remain substantial barriers. The UPMEM study identifies robust system software and unified virtual memory across processing units as research directions. The broader target needs effective placement of data and work, coordination across processing regions, and practical support for complete programs. These requirements do not mandate a particular operating-system design. They require evidence that the chosen software and hardware work together without transferring the dominant cost elsewhere.

Evidence boundary: the supplied sources establish important partial capabilities and technical obstacles, but do not establish that the complete target remained absent worldwide on November 1, 2026. The missing breakthrough is therefore defined here as the capability still to be convincingly demonstrated within this record, rather than as a verified claim that no contemporary system could meet it.

current_state.text: The supplied March 7, 2024 arXiv version of “Pathfinding Future PIM Architectures by Demystifying a Commercial PIM Technology” documents UPMEM as a commercial, general-purpose, highly programmable processing-in-memory architecture. It provides concrete evidence that programmability near memory is already real. Its documented limitations include bank-local execution and host-mediated communication between processing units. These findings describe one architecture and should not be generalized into an exhaustive classification of every PIM design. The supplied version is an arXiv preprint; this record does not establish its subsequent publication history.

That study primarily investigates performance, and its simulator leaves power modeling for future work. Its finding that many local workloads shift from memory-bound to compute-bound execution is meaningful, but neither that shift nor the remaining communication overhead establishes the fraction of whole-system energy spent moving data. The supplied review used the complete 17-page paper text, including its conclusion and references; its figures were not visually inspected.

“Achieving high precision in analog in-memory computing systems,” published January 7, 2026 in npj Unconventional Computing, reviews experimental analog computing primitives and methods for improving their precision. It documents continuing tradeoffs among precision, complexity, area, and digital overhead, rather than a general-purpose stored-program machine meeting the proposed system-level target. The supplied review assessed article prose and captions retained in HTML, which omitted figure images and table contents. Although the source index also lists a saved PDF, the supplied review does not establish independent inspection of its detailed visual or tabular benchmarks. No numerical benchmark from those materials is inferred here.

The research identifies “Scalability Limitations of Processing-in-Memory using Real System Evaluations” as a February 21, 2024 ACM paper and identifies DOI 10.1145/3639046 as the full-paper reference. It attributes host-mediated communication limitations to that paper. However, no artifact for the ACM source was captured, so the supplied evidence review could not independently verify its identity or proposed quotation. That limitation does not show the reported result is false; the verified UPMEM text independently supports the narrower architectural communication limitation.

Taken together, these dated sources demonstrate constituent technologies and identify obstacles. They do not provide whole-system energy measurements across the proposed application suite, and they do not demonstrate achievement of the complete innovation. The supplied freshness record is empty, so the record also cannot establish a comprehensive state of the field as of November 1, 2026. This is a limit on the available assessment, not evidence that later progress did or did not occur.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed acceptance criterion: demonstrate complete programs spanning databases, graph analytics, scientific computing, and neural networks, with compiler targeting permitted. On each specified workload, data-movement energy should be below 20% of total system energy, and energy-delay product should improve by at least 10× against a documented, competitive conventional baseline performing the same task at matched output accuracy. These numbers are proposed targets, not published consensus standards or achieved results.
completion_criteria.label: Data-movement below 20% of system energy, energy-delay product 10× better

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement protocol: define the system boundary and account for host execution, communication, memory accesses, conversion, initialization, and required error mitigation. State how data-movement energy is separated from other consumption and report measurement uncertainty. Publish energy and execution time separately as well as their product, with results for every workload so an aggregate score cannot conceal failures. Any claimed throughput gain should be demonstrated directly.
completion_criteria.label: Full boundary account separating data-movement energy with per-workload uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed software demonstration: show the compiler, runtime, memory management, synchronization, and operating-system interfaces needed to execute the complete programs. Document host involvement and data placement, and include application-wide communication rather than measuring only local arithmetic. A single accelerated kernel would not meet this criterion, even if its isolated efficiency were exceptional.
completion_criteria.label: Full software stack runs complete programs with application-wide communication

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: provide the hardware configuration, software versions, programs, inputs, accuracy requirements, baseline tuning, and measurement procedures needed for independent reproduction. Establish how results change with problem size, communication intensity, precision, and operating conditions, and document reliability requirements and failure cases. A finite workload suite would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions; it would not prove literal universality or superiority on every program.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reproduction package with condition sensitivity and failure cases

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CPE-02, “Room-temperature general-purpose adiabatic reversible computer,” and CPE-06, “Wall-plug-superior superconducting classical computer at useful scale,” share the goal of more efficient general computing. Their titles identify different primary routes: reversible operation and superconducting implementation. CPE-03 concerns the energy of transporting data through a complete architecture. These approaches could be combined, but success on one target would not establish the others.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-04, “Cascadable general-purpose photonic computer with optical memory,” overlaps through its explicit integration of processing and memory. It additionally requires a photonic implementation with cascadability and optical storage. CPE-03 is neutral about the physical computing medium and instead requires measured removal of transport-energy dominance across diverse applications. Photonic hardware would still need to demonstrate that system-level outcome.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-05, “Mammalian-scale neuromorphic learning machine near biological energy,” overlaps through energy-efficient computation and potentially close coupling of stored state and processing. Its target centers on learning at a particular scale and energy level. CPE-03 requires broad application coverage beyond learning, so a neuromorphic learning achievement alone would not establish it.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-08, “Economically manufacturable atomic-density defect-tolerant digital computer,” could provide dense storage and processing resources relevant to this fabric. Its defining challenges concern density, defect tolerance, and manufacturability. Greater density does not by itself demonstrate efficient application-wide communication or low transport-energy consumption. Likewise, improved memory cells or additional stacking could contribute without establishing CPE-03.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-01, “Application-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer,” concerns reliable quantum computation, while CPE-07, “Utility-scale quantum-repeater internet,” concerns quantum networking. Neither title specifies CPE-03's broad programmable memory-compute architecture or its energy criterion. Data transport is relevant to many computing systems, but that shared concern does not merge these distinct targets. The research's references to historical items numbered 2 and 7 cannot be mapped to this roster without their missing descriptions.

brief.title: Computers that waste less energy moving data
possible: People could run large databases, analyse linked data, perform scientific calculations and use neural networks—computer models that learn patterns—with far less energy spent shuttling data around. A programmable computer would do the work within or close to where it stores the data.
why: Moving data between memory and processors consumes energy. Reducing that cost across complete programs could make large computing jobs more practical within power and cooling budgets.

sources.who: Piergiulio Mannocci, Giacomo Larelli, Marco Bonomi and Daniele Ielmini
sources.showed: Their review describes computing inside memory using physical electrical signals. It explains how errors can be reduced, alongside the extra circuitry and processing those corrections require.
sources.cited_for: Computing inside memory can support useful arithmetic, but accuracy improvements carry costs.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate a broadly programmable computer with low whole-system data-transfer energy.

sources.who: Bongjoon Hyun, Taehun Kim, Dongjae Lee and Minsoo Rhu at KAIST
sources.showed: The researchers built a simulator to study UPMEM’s commercial computer, which places programmable processors near stored data. Their preprint identifies limits in computation and communication.
sources.quote:
Our first key contribution is the
development of a flexible simulation framework for PIM.
sources.cited_for: Programmable processing near memory already exists, while coordination between processors remains a challenge.
sources.not_established: The study does not measure whole-system energy savings across the required application types.

sources.showed: This is a study of scaling limits in real systems that process data near memory.
sources.cited_for: It reports communication limits caused by routing exchanges through the main processor.
sources.not_established: It does not establish the broad application execution and whole-system energy savings required.

shown: UPMEM already sells programmable processors located near memory. The KAIST preprint shows that this arrangement can shift the limiting factor from accessing data to doing calculations. Communication between its processing units still passes through the main processor.

Experiments reviewed by Mannocci and colleagues demonstrate arithmetic inside memory. Methods can improve its accuracy, but they add costs. Neither line of work demonstrates the complete capability across the required applications.
missing: Complete programs still need to demonstrate broad energy savings after all communication and software costs are counted.
Processing units need to exchange data and coordinate without erasing the savings from working near memory.
Computing inside memory needs to retain its energy benefit while delivering the accuracy each application requires.

milestones.label: Low transfer energy and large overall efficiency gains
milestones.explanation: Complete database, linked-data, scientific and neural-network programs would have to keep data transfers below 20% of energy and meet the target for energy multiplied by runtime at matched accuracy. This would establish breadth.

milestones.label: Complete energy accounting for every workload
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to count the whole system, separate transfer energy and report uncertainty, energy and runtime for each program. This would reveal hidden costs and distinguish energy savings from speed gains.

milestones.label: Complete programs run with all supporting software
milestones.explanation: The software that translates and runs programs, manages memory and coordinates work would have to support complete applications, including communication throughout each program. This would establish benefits beyond isolated calculations.

milestones.label: Independent reproduction reveals practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce results and establish how size, communication, accuracy, operating conditions and failures affect them. This would define where the benefits hold.

uncertain: The application suite, measurement boundaries, acceptable uncertainty and comparison computers still need precise definitions.
Energy savings may not bring faster execution; calculation itself can become the limiting factor.
A successful application suite would demonstrate breadth within tested conditions, rather than superiority on every program.

page.title: Processing-in-memory with minority data-movement energy
page.definition: A programmable computer computes within or near stored data and runs complete database, graph-analytics, scientific-computing and neural-network applications. Data movement consumes less than 50% of whole-system execution energy for each application.

goal.need: A 2018 study examined four Google consumer workload classes, covering Chrome, TensorFlow Mobile, VP9 playback and VP9 capture. Its characterization used an Intel Celeron N3060 Chromebook with 2 GB of DRAM, hardware performance counters and energy modeling. The attributed data-movement energy shares quantify the energy budget that memory-centric computing targets.

figures.caption: Data-movement energy shares in the 2018 Google consumer-workload study.
figures.note: The model counts CPU cores, caches, DRAM and off-chip interconnects.

completion.title: A programmable PIM system spends under half its energy moving data across four application classes.
completion.criterion: One programmable processing-in-memory system runs at least one complete application in each of databases, graph analytics, scientific computing and neural networks. For every application, data-movement energy is <50% of total execution energy, and total energy is lower than for a conventional processor–memory baseline performing the same task at matched correctness or accuracy. Hardware measurements cover host execution, memory, interconnects, control, conversion and required error correction. Applications, inputs, accuracy targets and energy boundaries are fixed for the comparison.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas, working operational definition of data-movement energy dominance.
completion.basis: DARPA FRANC and OPTIMA, IEEE IRDS 2024 and PIM benchmark searches yielded no cross-application whole-system transport-energy threshold. This Atlas working test defines dominance as a majority of execution energy. The 50% boundary is an Atlas operational definition. The four application classes specify demonstrated breadth.

milestones.title: A processing-in-memory building-block prototype functions in execution tests.
milestones.criterion: A physical building-block prototype functions and completes its execution tests. FRANC specifies independent government testing using procedures agreed with each performer. Related near-memory evidence includes commercial programmable UPMEM processors described in the preprint revised on 7 March 2024. Related in-memory evidence includes experimentally demonstrated arithmetic and precision-correction primitives reviewed on 7 January 2026.
milestones.set_by: DARPA FRANC, HR001117S0056 Amendment 01, section I.C.5, TA-2 final-gate table on PDF page 26. This is a programme-specific component gate. Its threshold appears in a table.

milestones.title: A memory-centric prototype executes benchmarks with at least a tenfold gain on its chosen metric.
milestones.criterion: FRANC TA-1 requires a functioning integrated processing-and-memory prototype using new materials or integration processes, diverging from conventional von Neumann architecture and executing agreed benchmarks. Its performer-specified metric improves by at least 10× over the state of the art. Energy–delay product is permitted. Related near-memory results in the PrIM preprint include 23.2× mean speedup over an Intel Xeon CPU across 16 benchmarks using 2,556 processing units. Related in-memory hardware includes a 64-core phase-change-memory chip with 256 × 256 arrays per core. These publications provide evidence of prototypes and benchmarking. Their FRANC acceptance remains unverified.
milestones.set_by: DARPA FRANC, HR001117S0056 Amendment 01, sections I.C.3 and I.C.5, TA-1. The target applies to programme prototypes using new materials or integration technologies.
milestones.threshold_quote: the completed system must advance over the current state of the art by at least a factor of ten

milestones.title: A programmable PIM system reduces whole-system energy in each of four application classes.
milestones.criterion: One programmable PIM system completes at least one application in each of databases, graph analytics, scientific computing and neural networks, with lower total execution energy than a conventional task- and accuracy-matched baseline. The boundary includes host, memory, communication, control and precision-recovery overheads. Near-memory evidence includes PrIM's PIM-chip energy measurements and the 2024 ACM study's two communication-intensive workloads. The in-memory review documents precision-recovery overheads. Whole-application qualification remains open in these sources.
milestones.set_by: Atlas working milestone. Searches of DARPA FRANC, IEEE IRDS and PIM benchmarks found no published cross-domain whole-application energy gate.
